item.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Hospitality and Tourism
item.content:encoded:
Hyunsu Kim, University of Macau

Kevin Kam Fung So, Purdue University

Ying Wang, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University

Emily Ma, University of Surrey

The hospitality and tourism industry is undergoing rapid transformation driven by artificial intelligence, which now collaborates with humans across diverse applications from restaurants to airlines. This human-AI partnership combines machine learning efficiency with human creativity and contextual understanding to reshape service delivery and customer experiences. The integration of AI in functions like personalized recommendations, dynamic pricing, and concierge services requires careful consideration of how to balance operational gains with meaningful human connections.

This special issue invites research on effective, ethical, and sustainable human-AI collaboration in hospitality and tourism contexts. The collection seeks empirical evidence and frameworks that help organizations design services combining operational efficiency with human-centered value. Contributions should address how such collaboration affects guest experiences, employee well-being, destination competitiveness, accessibility, and sustainability across various hospitality sectors including accommodations, food and beverage, attractions, and destination management.

item.title: Conceptualizing and Defining Public Service Delivery Hubs
item.content:encoded:
Steven Parker, Open University

Kate Broadhurst, Loughborough University

Public service hubs are organizational arrangements bringing together multiple services and professionals to address complex social challenges. Despite their growing adoption, these hubs remain poorly conceptualized and theoretically underdeveloped. The special issue seeks to advance understanding of what constitutes a hub, how it differs from other collaborative forms, and what value it creates.

The call particularly welcomes research examining financial and resourcing dimensions of hub working, including funding mechanisms, commissioning, and value-for-money evaluations. Submissions should critically explore hub design, implementation, governance, and evaluation, acknowledging the diversity of models ranging from specialist to inclusive arrangements, and including emerging digital variants. Contributions may draw on various theoretical frameworks and examine hubs internationally using alternative terminology.

The journal invites practitioner-academic collaborations and welcomes debate and new development formats alongside research articles.

Appel publié par Public Money & Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
